title: Levothyroxine in women with thyroid peroxidase antibodies before conception
authors: Dhillon-Smith RK, Middleton LJ, Sunner KK, Cheed V, Baker K, Farrell-Carver S, et al.
followUp: from before conception to the end of pregnancy
population: Euthyroid women with thyroid peroxidase antibodies and a history of miscarriage or infertility, from 19,585 women tested at 49 UK hospitals
funder: Supported by the United Kingdom NIHR efficacy and mechanism evaluation program (project number 09/100/10). Generic levothyroxine and placebo were packaged and supplied by Sharp HealthCare (formerly Bilcare United Kingdom), which had no role in the design of the trial; the collection, analysis or interpretation of the data.
authorConflicts: Disclosure forms are available with the full text at NEJM.org; not read.
result: Levothyroxine 50 µg daily or placebo. Live birth after at least 34 weeks: 176 of 470 (37.4%) against 178 of 470 (37.9%); relative risk 0.97 (95% CI 0.83 to 1.14), absolute difference -0.4 percentage points (-6.6 to 5.8). Pregnancy loss, preterm birth and neonatal outcomes did not differ. Serious adverse events in 28 women (5.9%) on levothyroxine and 18 (3.8%) on placebo (P = 0.14).
